title: Connect Claude Code to WordPress with MCP (Then Lock It Down)

notes.tone: Practical and personal, a British YouTuber talking to WordPress developers. Clean screen recordings at readable zoom (code at 1080p must be legible). Light, low music bed under the walkthroughs; drop it out for the SSH story (b35 to b40) and bring it back at b41. Captions on. Recurring graphics: numbered chapter cards for steps 1 to 5 in one style, and the kitchen illustration (hatch, jars, padlocks, key) built once and reused in b15 to b18, b33 and b37. On-screen text in British English, no em dashes. Zooms are simple punch-ins, not animated swoops.
notes.before_timeline: Fact-check flags from the script: (1) Check what discover-abilities actually lists before filming so 'apart from what WordPress and WooCommerce already expose' (sentence 102) is honest. (2) Confirm mcp-adapter.zip on the Releases page is still the latest release on the day (v0.6.1 at time of writing). (3) '${VAR}' expansion needs the variables set in the shell that launches Claude Code; the on-screen note in b26 covers this, keep it. (4) The Shop Manager order answers (b32) must visibly come through MCP tool calls, not a fallback route. (5) The SSH transcript (b36) must be the real one, on screen. (6) 'Being assessed for the plugin directory' (sentence 27) is hearsay unless you have a source; link one if you can. Plus from this edit: script cue 9 says 'then terminal' but v2 installs from the Releases zip, so the terminal is only needed for the optional build aside in b12. Script cue 20 asks for the finished file at sentence 61, before LOG_FILE is described in sentence 66, so the finished file is held in b26 instead. Sentence 98 says permissions can deny SSH commands outright; Wordmove runs ssh itself, so the on-screen deny list in b39 should cover wordmove, scp and rsync as well as ssh or the claim is weaker than it sounds. Check 'Claude Cowork' (sentence 112) is the product name you mean.

notes.description: Paste the finished .mcp.json from script cue 22 into the YouTube description (or link a Gist), as the pinned comment promises. Chapter timestamps come from the beat chapters.
notes.end_screen: Last 20 seconds (b62): presenter framed left, end screen elements on the right, the main one being the anchor video on the Abilities API theory.
notes.split_option: The audience brief says the ability build is optional detail. b47 to b61 (sec11 and sec12) can be lifted out as its own video, with b46 'Let's build it.' as the cut point, if the runtime needs trimming.

sections.purpose: Hook with the SSH breakout, set up the gap in the official docs, and define MCP in one line. Fast and personal.
Step one: create a dedicated user on the live site with the lowest role. Practical, with the 'don't give it admin' warning landing clearly.
Step two: generate an application password for that user. Practical; blur the password.
Step three: install the MCP Adapter from GitHub Releases, then show that none of the pieces does anything on its own yet.
The insight: the kitchen analogy (hatch, jars, padlocks, key). Slower and illustrated; this is what people should remember.
Step four: build .mcp.json line by line with environment variables. The most rewatched section, so every line must be readable and the finished file held.
Step five: start Claude Code, prove the connection, and recap the checklist. Payoff.
Show that the role controls what the AI can reach, then put the role back. Quick demo.
Pay off the cold open: the SSH story, then CLAUDE.md plus permissions. Serious, no music until it's done.
The real use case: CasaGees delivery slots and why an ability fixes the weekly chore. Lighter again.
Honest framing that AI wrote the ability, then the main plugin file and the permission callback. Could be split into its own video.
Tour of the ability file: registration, callbacks, schemas and the easy-to-miss mcp public flag.
Sign-off with the end screen pointing to the anchor video.
